wa_exit_32_little_si.blurb: Little Si is a small peak below Mount Si just outside North Bend, in the Central-West Cascades and a short drive from Seattle. The crags sit on its northeast side. Sport climbing dominates, backed by a block of bouldering plus a modest number of trad lines and top-ropes. The grades lean hard: most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.13, with a smaller set of easier climbs at 5.9 and below, and the boulder problems run from V0 into the V10 range. The rock is volcanic metamorphic stone, from grippy and textured to slick and sharp, and it is mostly clean. World Wall is the headline, a gently overhanging face with many linkups, while the British Aisles and the Woods add variety. Most crags face northeast and stay shaded, which makes late spring a good time to visit.

ca_auburn_and_grass_valley.blurb: This is a scattering of short rocks and boulders in the Gold Country foothills of California, mostly along and near Highway 49 around Auburn and Grass Valley. Rather than one big cliff, it is a collection of small crags and boulder clusters tucked among rivers and canyons at low elevation. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with problems from V0 up into V9, mostly in the easy and middle grades. Sport routes come next, running from about 5.9 to 5.12, with a handful of top-ropes, trad lines and aid climbs. Auburn State Recreation Area holds the most climbs: a quarry area carries much of the sport climbing, and The Bar is a well-known boulder zone. The South Yuba River crossings, Hirschman's Pond and Dutch Creek Falls add more boulders.

vt_3_southern_vermont.blurb: Southern Vermont is, above all, a bouldering region, with only a few ice, trad and top-rope lines on the side. Bromley Forest holds most of the problems, in the woods off Route 11/30 above Manchester Center, on high-quality gneiss with a good run of moderates and plenty of hard problems. Road noise carries to some of the boulders. Jamaica is a quieter mix of boulders, top-ropes and a little trad, and smaller clusters such as Rooftopia and Ice Beds fill out the rest. Grades span V0 to V12, with the bulk between V0 and V6 and a thin tail of harder lines. Expect a woodland feel rather than big crags, with scattered boulders spread across several small areas.

wy_eastern_big_horns.blurb: The Eastern Big Horns run along the eastern flank of the Big Horn Mountains in north-central Wyoming, around Sheridan. Climbing is spread over canyons and roadside outcrops rather than concentrated in one place, with a quiet, scenic feel. Sport routes are the most common, then trad, with some bouldering and a little ice. Most routes sit between 5.9 and 5.12, with fewer easy climbs and a handful at 5.13. Dolomite is the predominant stone, Tongue River Canyon's walls are limestone, and a few granite zones have been developed. Piney Creek Canyon is the sport-heavy canyon for 5.10 to 5.12, with pockets of shade that help in summer. Tongue River Canyon mixes trad and sport on south-facing walls that run hot in summer, and crowds are light.

az_sedona.blurb: Sedona is a high-desert town in northern Arizona, roughly 30 miles south of Flagstaff on the southern edge of the Colorado Plateau. The climbing is mostly trad on red sandstone spires, towers and buttes, with sport routes gathered at Twin Butte and the Midgley Bridge area. Grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11, with a good number of 5.9 and below and a smaller group of 5.12 and 5.13 climbs. Many outings are multi-pitch. The sandstone is soft and quality varies from route to route, so expect some grit, and the rock is fragile when wet, which makes dry weather matter. Other zones include Marg's Draw, Mormon Canyon and the Cathedral Rock area. The setting is scenic but busy with visitors.

_expect.name: Twin Falls and the Snake River Canyon

id_twin_falls_and_the_snake_river_canyon.blurb: Climbing here lines the Snake River Canyon around Twin Falls in south-central Idaho. The upper canyon is stacked basalt lava flows, and the walls are mostly vertical to very steep, with overhangs, cracks, edges and pockets. Sport climbing and bouldering dominate, with a few trad lines and some top-ropes. Sport routes run mostly from 5.8 to 5.11, with a smaller group of 5.12 and a few harder ones, while boulder problems lean toward V0 to V5. Dierkes Lake holds most of the climbing, with Shoshone Falls, Gawker Wall, Picnic Crag and Auger Falls Park adding more. Auger Falls is described as friendly for beginners and families. A few crags also form ice in cold winters.
